summary: @servicetitan/confirm preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs downloads a Bun v1.3.13 binary for the installer's platform/arch from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to the OS temp directory, chmods it executable, and execFileSyncs it to run the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727,680-byte single-line obfuscated Bun-CJS bundle (rotated string-array indirection via WV8StW over n7gIxM, _0x-style identifiers, no readable strings or endpoints). The package advertises itself as a React confirmation-dialog component; nothing in that documented purpose requires fetching an alternate JavaScript runtime at install and executing an opaque bundle through it. Because the payload is executed by Bun rather than Node, its behavior is not observable to Node-based tooling at install time. The pattern — preinstall lifecycle hook, external runtime pulled from a non-registry host, and an obfuscated local blob executed by that runtime — matches the alternate-runtime-dropper shape and fires automatically on default npm install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
